source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only once when the employee is first hired, because annual retraining is not required after the initial occupational-exposure instruction.","B":"At initial assignment to tasks with occupational exposure and at least annually thereafter, with additional training when required.","C":"Every five years after the initial course, because the bloodborne-pathogens standard uses a five-year refresher interval.","D":"Only after a documented exposure incident, because routine annual education is optional when no needlestick or splash has occurred."}}
source_row.rationale: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires that employees with occupational exposure risk receive training initially upon assignment to tasks with exposure risk, and then at least annually thereafter, ensuring ongoing awareness of safe practices and updated information.
source_row.source_detail: 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(ii)(A)-(B) and (v): training at initial assignment and at least annually; additional training for changes in tasks/procedures affecting exposure. Current OSHA regulation reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
